claims.text: A model incorporating atomic-level disorder metrics and local lattice-distortion descriptors will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than models based mainly on average compositional properties.
High-entropy alloys inherently exhibit lattice disorder.
Phonon scattering dominates thermal transport in the relevant temperature range from approximately room temperature to 600 K.
Atomic mass fluctuation and local strain can quantify atomic-scale disorder and lattice distortion.
Significant compositional disorder enhances phonon scattering.
Local lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces thermal conductivity.
Integrating disorder and lattice-distortion descriptors allows the proposed model to capture the stated phonon-scattering mechanism.
The proposed model will produce a statistically significant increase in prediction accuracy or decrease in prediction error relative to traditional models.
Existing baseline models rely mainly on averaged compositional or elemental data and omit detailed disorder metrics.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys with sufficient compositional complexity.
The approach may have limited predictive capability for alloys with less disorder or for ordered intermetallic compounds.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can be used to obtain the experimental phonon thermal-conductivity values required by the benchmark.
